title: Email Management, Attachments, and Organization
description: Organize your inbox with labels, stars, filters, and practice searching and managing emails
objective: Students will organize their Gmail inbox using labels, stars, and filters, practice searching with Gmail operators, and manage contacts.

steps.title: Create Labels to Organize Emails
steps.instructions:
1. Open **Gmail** in your web browser
2. In the left sidebar, scroll down and click **More** to expand all options
3. Scroll to the bottom of the sidebar and click **Create new label**
4. Create the following **three labels** one by one:
   - Label 1: `CCC Studies`
   - Label 2: `Personal`
   - Label 3: `Important Docs`
5. After creating all three labels, they should appear in the left sidebar
6. Now apply a label to an email:
   - Go to your **Inbox**
   - Right-click on any email
   - Select **Label as** → check `CCC Studies`
   - The label tag now appears on the email
7. Click the `CCC Studies` label in the sidebar — your labeled email should appear there
8. **Try this:** Apply multiple labels to the same email (right-click → Label as → check both `CCC Studies` and `Important Docs`)

**CCC Exam Fact:** Labels in Gmail work like tags — one email can have multiple labels. Labels are similar to folders but more flexible.

steps.title: Star Important Emails and Use Folders
steps.instructions:
1. Go to your **Inbox**
2. Find the first email you sent during Lab 07A
3. Click the **star icon** (hollow star) next to the email — it turns yellow
4. Star two more emails in your Inbox
5. In the left sidebar, click **Starred** — verify all three starred emails appear
6. Now explore the other default folders:
   - Click **Sent Mail** — see all emails you have sent
   - Click **Drafts** — this should be empty (unless you have unsent emails)
   - Click **Spam** — check if any emails were automatically filtered as spam
   - Click **Trash** — check for any deleted emails
   - Click **All Mail** — see every email in your account
7. **Delete an email:** Go to Inbox, select an email using the checkbox, click the **trash icon**
8. Go to **Trash** — verify the deleted email is there
9. **Recover it:** Open the email in Trash, click **Move to** → **Inbox**

**CCC Exam Fact:** Deleted emails go to **Trash** and are automatically deleted permanently after **30 days**. Spam emails are also deleted after **30 days**.

steps.title: Search Emails Using Gmail Operators
steps.instructions:
1. Click the **Search bar** at the top of Gmail
2. Practice these search operators one by one:

   **Search 1:** Type `from:me` and press Enter
   - This shows all emails **sent by you**
   - Count how many emails appear

   **Search 2:** Type `has:attachment` and press Enter
   - This shows all emails that have **file attachments**
   - You should see the email with `my_profile.txt` from Lab 07A

   **Search 3:** Type `subject:CCC` and press Enter
   - This shows all emails with **"CCC" in the subject line**

   **Search 4:** Type `is:starred` and press Enter
   - This shows all **starred emails**

   **Search 5:** Type `is:unread` and press Enter
   - This shows all **unread emails**

3. Try the **advanced search**: Click the small arrow on the right side of the search bar
   - This opens advanced search with fields for From, To, Subject, Has words, Has attachment, Date
   - Fill in "Has the words" with `practice` and click **Search**

4. Write down in your notebook: Which search operator was most useful to you and why?

**CCC Exam Fact:** Gmail search operators help you find specific emails quickly. Important operators: `from:`, `to:`, `subject:`, `has:attachment`, `is:unread`, `is:starred`.

steps.title: Create a Filter for Automatic Organization
steps.instructions:
1. Click the **search bar dropdown arrow** (small triangle icon on the right side of the search bar)
2. In the **From** field, type your trainer's email address
3. Click **Create filter** (at the bottom right of the dropdown)
4. In the filter options, check the following:
   - **Apply the label:** Select `CCC Studies` from the dropdown
   - **Star it:** Check this box
   - **Also apply filter to matching conversations:** Check this box
5. Click **Create filter**
6. Now, every email from your trainer will automatically:
   - Get the `CCC Studies` label
   - Be starred

7. **Test the filter:** Ask your trainer to send you a test email, or send yourself an email from another account. Verify the label and star are applied automatically.

8. **Manage Filters:**
   - Go to **Settings** (gear icon) → **See all settings** → **Filters and Blocked Addresses** tab
   - Here you can see, edit, or delete your filters

**CCC Exam Fact:** Filters automatically sort incoming emails based on rules you set (sender, subject, keywords). This is a powerful inbox management tool.

steps.title: Manage Contacts (Address Book)
steps.instructions:
1. Open a new browser tab and go to **contacts.google.com**
   (Or click the **Google Apps** grid icon in Gmail and select **Contacts**)
2. Click **Create contact** (the + icon)
3. Add a new contact with these details:
   - **First name:** Priya
   - **Last name:** Sharma
   - **Email:** priya.sharma.demo@gmail.com
   - **Phone:** 9876543210
   - **Company:** TechPath Institute
4. Click **Save**
5. Add two more contacts for classmates (use their real names and email addresses)
6. **Create a Contact Group (Label):**
   - In Google Contacts, click **Labels** in the left sidebar
   - Click **Create label**
   - Name it: `CCC Classmates`
   - Select your classmates' contacts and add them to this group
7. **Test Auto-Complete:**
   - Go back to Gmail and click **Compose**
   - In the **To** field, start typing `Priya` — Gmail should suggest Priya Sharma's email
   - This is the auto-complete feature powered by your Contacts
8. Close the compose window without sending

**CCC Exam Fact:** The address book (Contacts) stores email addresses for quick access. Gmail auto-suggests contacts when you type in the To, CC, or BCC fields.
